notes.ios:
RefineID is a smart-card driver. It makes the certificates on a Finnish identity card (FINEID) available to the operating system, so Safari can use them to sign in to Finnish public e-services at suomi.fi, the government's national service portal. It also signs PDF documents with the card's qualified signature certificate.

There is no account to demonstrate. The app has no login, no RefineID cloud service, no registration, and collects no data. Nothing in it sits behind credentials, so there is no user name and password we can supply: none exists.

What the app needs is the card itself. The identity card is a legal identity document issued by the Finnish Police to one named citizen, in the same category as a passport; the certificates on it are issued by the Finnish Digital and Population Data Services Agency. It cannot be duplicated, transferred, or issued for testing, so we are unable to put one in the reviewer's hands.

VIRTUAL ID CARD - DEMONSTRATION MODE

In place of a card, this build carries a Virtual ID Card: an explicit, fictional identity card whose state a reviewer can inspect and edit. Every number on it is fictional and public in the source.

1. Press and hold the RefineID icon on the Home Screen and choose "Demo Mode". "DEMO MODE" is shown at the bottom of the screen for as long as the mode is on, and a red floating "Virtual ID Card" button stays on screen.
2. The app starts with an activated fictional card. Its numbers: card access number 123456, PIN 1 1234, PIN 2 123456, PUK 12345678. Walk the ordinary setup with them - enter the card access number and read the certificate. The screen then names the fictional holder, DOE JANE 12345678N. Activating a factory-fresh card is not part of this release; a card in that state is shown a notice saying so, and the editor below can demonstrate it.
3. Tap the red Virtual ID Card button to open the card editor. It selects named card states - factory fresh, partially activated, activated, registered, and recovery states with low or blocked counters - and edits every value the UI reacts to: transport (NFC or reader), card presence, PIN 1, PIN 2 and PUK retry counters, certificate states, and one deterministic injected fault such as a lost connection or a card removed mid-operation.
4. The ordinary product screens handle whatever is configured: PIN 1 and PIN 2 change, PIN reset with the PUK 12345678, the refusal that protects a card on its last two attempts, and qualified signing of a supplied fictional PDF with PIN 2 123456.

Demo Mode lasts one launch: only the Home Screen action turns it on, so no ordinary launch can enter it, and quitting the app ends it. Nothing in it touches a card or the system. No certificate is read, nothing is stored, no token is registered, and no output can be mistaken for a genuine card signature: the fictional holder has no certificate, so the system is offered no identity.

Also verifiable without a card:
- Every screen is available in English, Finnish and Swedish, and with VoiceOver, larger text, and the dark interface. The fictional holder is named in each language.
- The camera button beside the card access number opens a scanner for the QR code printed on the card.

With a real card, this build reads the card over the iPhone's NFC antenna or a connected USB-C smart-card reader, publishes the card's certificates to the system for Safari, and signs PDF documents with PIN 2.

The complete source is public at https://github.com/ReFineID/ReFineID-Apple, including the card protocol and the whole Virtual ID Card harness, so the behaviour behind the card can be read directly.
notes.macos:
RefineID is a smart-card driver. It makes the certificates on a Finnish identity card (FINEID) available to the operating system, so Safari can use them to sign in to Finnish public e-services at suomi.fi, the government's national service portal. It also signs PDF documents with the card's qualified signature certificate.

There is no account to demonstrate. The app has no login, no RefineID cloud service, no registration, and collects no data. Nothing in it sits behind credentials, so there is no user name and password we can supply: none exists.

What the app needs is the card itself. The identity card is a legal identity document issued by the Finnish Police to one named citizen, in the same category as a passport; the certificates on it are issued by the Finnish Digital and Population Data Services Agency. It cannot be duplicated, transferred, or issued for testing, so we are unable to put one in the reviewer's hands.

Verifiable without a card, on this build:
- The app launches and reports "Present your identity card to the reader" rather than failing.
- The bundled direct-reader CryptoTokenKit extension registers with the system on first launch and appears in the smart-card system driver list with no card present. A separate persistent-token extension represents a cryptographically paired iPhone without replacing or changing the reader driver.
- Settings contains the PIN pane, which shows the card's change and reset tasks and its attempt counters, and the time-stamp authority list used when signing a document.
- Every screen is available in English, Finnish and Swedish, and with VoiceOver, larger text, and the dark interface.

If a card is inserted into a reader, macOS itself may offer to pair the card for system login; that sheet belongs to the operating system and can be dismissed. Direct reader use needs no operating-system card pairing. Using an iPhone as the card authorizer uses a separate explicit in-app RAPP pairing.

The app makes outbound Internet connections only when an archival document signature fetches a qualified time stamp and revocation data. It also advertises and accepts the local-network RAPP service used by a cryptographically paired iPhone. Every remote card operation requires explicit approval on the iPhone; CAN, PIN 1, and PIN 2 never cross to the Mac. There is no cloud relay or RefineID backend. The first authenticated protocol violation, rejected card credential, or ambiguous card completion tears down the pairing and requires manual pairing again.

The iOS build of the same version carries a demonstration mode, the Virtual ID Card, described in the iOS review notes. If a demonstration mode is expected on macOS as well, please say so and we will add one.
The complete source is public at https://github.com/ReFineID/ReFineID-Apple, including the card protocol, so the behaviour behind the card can be read directly.

promotionalText.macos: Log in to services with your identity card and sign documents.
promotionalText.ios: Log in to services with your identity card and sign documents.

description.macos:
A reader for the Finnish identity card.

Insert your identity card into a USB smart-card reader and sign in to e-services directly in Safari with the certificate on your card. Drop a PDF on RefineID to sign it with a qualified signature.

RefineID is open source: github.com/ReFineID/ReFineID-Apple
description.ios:
RefineID brings the Finnish identity card to iPhone.

Read your card with a USB-C smart-card reader, or wirelessly on iPhone, then sign in to e-services directly in Safari with the certificate on your card. Pick a PDF in RefineID to sign it with a qualified signature.

RefineID is open source: github.com/ReFineID/ReFineID-Apple
